title: Isolation, culture, and immunostaining of neonatal rat ventricular myocytes
protocol: Sterilize scissors (one curved; one straight) and forceps.
Transfer 20 mL of 1× ADS buffer into each of two sterile 100 mm dishes placed on ice.
Prepare 60 mL of Collagenase Buffer in a 100 mL sterile beaker.
Filter 15 mL of Collagenase Buffer with a 0.22 μm filter using a syringe in a 100 mL sterile laboratory bottle.
Rinse neonatal rats aged 1–3 days old quickly in 75% ethanol solution for surface sterilization.
Decapitate the pups using sterile scissors (straight).
Open the chest along the sternum to access the heart cavity and heart.
Extract hearts from the body with curved scissors and transfer immediately into a dish containing ∼20 mL of 1× ADS buffer.
Remove lung tissue, large vessels, and atria from the heart.
Rinse the heart in 1× ADS solution to remove blood.
Transfer the heart to a second 100 mm dish containing 1× ADS to remove any additional blood.
Cut the hearts into 4–5 pieces directly into the Schott containing 10 mL of filtered Collagenase Buffer.
Incubate the heart tissue with the collagenase solution under continuous agitation at 180 rpm and 37°C for 60 minutes.
Check the cardiac tissue digestion; it should be almost complete after approximately 60 minutes.
For cardiomyocyte enrichment, perform a discontinuous Percoll gradient centrifugation.
Incubate the heart tissue with the collagenase solution under continuous agitation at 180 rpm and 37°C for an additional 10 minutes after the initial digestion step.
Use a sterile 10 mL serological pipette to pipette up and down 10 times to homogenize the sample and improve tissue dissociation.
Allow tissues to settle by gravity for 1 min, collect supernatant (approximately 11 mL), and transfer to 50 mL conical tubes.
Add 10 mL 0.22 μm filtered Collagenase Buffer solution to remaining cardiac tissue, and incubate under 180 rpm agitation at 37°C for 10 min.
Remove Schott from the 37°C shaker after enzymatic degradation is complete, add 1 mL of fetal bovine serum to the supernatant in the conical tube, and centrifuge at 2,000×g for 5 min at 25°C.
Carefully discard supernatant and add 2 mL of fetal bovine serum to cell pellet; homogenize pipetting up and down using a serological pipette.
Transfer cell suspension to a sterilized 100 mm glass petri dish (non-treated) for fibroblasts adhesion, incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for at least 1 h.
Repeat digestion, centrifugation, and pre-plating process with remaining tissue fragments 4-5 times.
Transfer supernatant of all five Petri dishes into a 50 mL conical tube after finishing the last digestion cycle.
Gently wash the Petri dishes with 6 mL fetal bovine serum and transfer the supernatant to one conical tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 2,000×g for 10 min at 25°C.
Resuspend the cells in 3 mL of 1× ADS buffer.
Prepare the two-layers Percoll gradient in a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Load 4 mL of low-density Percoll solution on top of 4 mL of high-density Percoll solution in each of four tubes, tilting the tube to avoid mixing.
Load up to 1 mL of cell suspension on the top layer of the Percoll gradient, tilting the tube during loading.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1,800×g for 45 min at 25°C with acceleration and deceleration switched off completely.
Carefully discard the high-density Percoll layer or non-cardiomyocytes using a sterile 5 mL pipette.
Collect the band corresponding to the NRVMs located at the interface of the low and high-density gradients.
Transfer the collected band containing NRVMs to a further 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Repeat this procedure with the remaining centrifuged tubes.
Combine them into the same 50 mL conical tube.
Add 30 mL of 1× ADS buffer.
Centrifuge the 50 mL tube at 1,800×g for 10 min at 25°C.
Discard the supernatant in a waste container.
Gently resuspend the cell pellet by pipetting 30 mL of 1× ADS buffer.
Repeat the previous wash step (centrifuge and discard supernatant).
Resuspend the pellet with 5 mL of warm Plating Culture Medium by gently pipetting to ensure a homogeneous solution of single cells.
Take 10 μL of resuspended cells into a new 1.5 mL tube.
Add 10 μL of 0.4% trypan blue dye solution.
Mix gently.
Load 10 μL of the mixture into the well of the Neubauer counting chamber.
Determine the total number of viable cells using a microscope focused on the grid of the Neubauer counting chamber.
Add 3 mL of fresh Plating Culture Medium per 35 mm dish or per well in a 6-well plate.
Plate the cells on the double-coated surface.
For immunostaining, place coverslips in dishes or wells to achieve 70–80% confluence with 500,000 cells.
Before plating, add Bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU) at a final concentration of 100 μM if desired.
Incubate the plates at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Forty-eight hours after plating, gently change the medium with 3 mL of Maintaining Culture Medium.
Remove non-attached cells during the medium exchange procedure.
Confirm that NRVMs are attached and exhibit spontaneous beating using a microscope.
At this point, perform any treatment, transfection, or virus transduction according to the experimental design.
Remove the medium and rinse briefly in 1× phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS pH 7.4 for 30 min on ice.
Incubate cells with 1% BSA, 50 mM glycine in PBS.
Wash three times for 5 min with 1× ice-cold PBS.
Permeabilize and block unspecific antibody binding by incubating the cell with 1% BSA, 0.1% Triton-X100, 50 mM glycine in PBS for 30 min.
Wash three times for 5 min with 1× PBS.
Incubate cells with primary antibodies (1:200 dilution) in 1% BSA in PBS overnight at 4°C.
Wash three times for 5 min with 1× PBS.
Incubate cells with Alexa Fluor-conjugated secondary antibody (1:200) for 2 h at room temperature.
Wash three times for 5 min with 1× PBS.
If applied, perform the cytosolic staining with phalloidin (1:50) for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash for 5 min with 1× PBS.
Incubate with nuclear stain DAPI (1:500) at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Wash for 5 min with 1× PBS.
Place the coverslip onto a drop of mounting media (Vectashield) with cells facing the slide.
Seal the coverslip with nail polish by gently outlining the perimeter of the slide.
